new_statements.quote: Nada adalah tinggi rendahnya suara dalam mengucapkan suatu ujaran, kata, frasa atau kalimat. Tekanan merupakan keras atau lembutnya suatu ucapan, sedangkan panjang adalah kualitas suatu bunyi. Ketiga jenis fonem suprasegmental ini dimiliki oleh BL. Ketiganya tidak mengubah arti kata BL, tetapi akan menimbulkan kejanggalan jika seseorang menggunakan nada tinggi rendah suara, tekanan suara, dan panjang pendek suatu fonem tidak pada tempatnya. Dalam ujaran yang lebih besar daripada kata, misalnya frasa dan kalimat maka nada, tekanan, dan panjang dapat mengubah arti. [p. 3:] Dalam bahasa Indonesia dan bahasa Lematang, tekanan tidak membedakan arti kata.
new_statements.translation: Pitch is the height of the voice in pronouncing an utterance, word, phrase or sentence. Stress is the loudness or softness of an utterance, while length is the quality [duration] of a sound. Lematang (BL) has all three of these suprasegmental phonemes. None of the three changes the meaning of a Lematang word, but it will sound odd if someone uses pitch, stress, or the length of a phoneme in the wrong place. In utterances larger than the word, e.g. phrases and sentences, pitch, stress and length can change meaning. [p. 3:] In Indonesian and in Lematang, stress does not distinguish word meaning.
new_statements.citation: Ihsan, Diemroh, Salamah Arifin, Agus Saripudin & Chuzaimah Dahlan Diem. 1996. Fonologi dan Morfologi Bahasa Lematang. Jakarta: Pusat Pembinaan dan Pengembangan Bahasa.
new_statements.locator: §3.5 Fonem Supra Segmental, p. 46 (p. 61); second sentence from §1.3.1, p. 3 (p. 18); restated in the conclusion, p. 127

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File opened: (145 pp., scan with scanned text; hard link of copy). Locators verified with extracted text: p. 61 carries printed page number 46 and the heading "3.5 Fonem Supra Segmental"; p. 18 carries printed p. 3. The quoted passage is present at p. 61 exactly as reported, differing only in scanned artefacts the compiler normalised ("lembutnnya" -> "lembutnya", "Ketigajenis" -> "Ketiga jenis", "pad a" -> "pada"); the p. 3 sentence reads in the scanned "Dalam bahasa Indonesia dan bahasa Lema[ang. [ekanan tidak membedakan arti kata" = "Dalam bahasa Indonesia dan bahasa Lematang, tekanan tidak membedakan arti kata". One locator correction: the conclusion restatement ("Keenam, BL.. juga menge…
new_statements.rule_in_words: The source states that Lematang has stress (together with pitch and length) but that it is non-contrastive at the word level: putting it in the wrong place merely sounds odd ('tidak pada tempatnya' implies stress has a normal place, but that place is never stated). Only juncture is treated as phonemic. No placement rule, no examples of stress marking, no mention of penultimate or final syllable anywhere in the book. The label 'unclear or contradictory' is used only because the fixed list has no 'non-contrastive, placement unstated' value; the statement itself is clear.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the only qualification is that above the word (phrase, sentence) pitch, stress and length can change meaning, which the authors assign to intonation and to morphology/syntax rather than phonology.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level ('arti kata'); phrase/sentence-level effects are explicitly separated as intonation. Data: five native speakers of Kec. Gunung Megang, Kab. Muara Enim (p. 6), i.e. Lematang Ilir.
new_statements.identity_note: lema1244 is a Glottolog bookkeeping entry for retired ISO 639-3 [lmt], merged into Musi [mui] by change request 2007-182 (Anderbeck). The only descriptive source, Ihsan et al. 1996, describes Lematang Ilir as spoken in Kec. Gunung Megang and Kec. Rambang Dangku, Kab. Muara Enim (pp. 7-8: two subdialects, Gunung Megang and Tanjung); it explicitly excludes Lematang Ulu (Kec. Merapi, Kab. Lahat), which is Besemah. This corresponds to Glottolog dialect lema1245 'Lematang Ilir' under Musi (musi1241); McDowell & Anderbeck 2020 pp. 16-17 place it in the Palembang-Lowland cluster of Musi and note it might better be called Lematang Tengah. The same file is already held under musi1241/ and was used there for the Musi check; any catalog entry should be filed under musi1241/lema1245 rather than as a separate language.

sources.locator: §3.5 Fonem Supra Segmental, p. 46 (p. 61); second sentence from §1.3.1, p. 3 (p. 18); restated in the conclusion, p. 127
sources.note: p. 3: in Indonesian and Lematang stress does not distinguish word meaning; §3.5 Fonem Supra Segmental p. 46: pitch, stress and length exist in Lematang but do not change word meaning (misplacing them only sounds odd); above the word they act as intonation; only juncture is phonemic (four juncture types, pp. 46-47). Conclusion p. 127 repeats this. No placement rule anywhere. p. 2: no prior study of Lematang existed.

sources.note: Only two linguistic records on Lematang surfaced: Ihsan et al. 1996 and Sari et al. 2025 (both opened). No 'Struktur Bahasa Lematang' or any other Pusat Bahasa / Balai Bahasa description of Lematang appears in the captured Kemdikbud repository or Open Library; the earlier scan's guessed title is unverified and contradicted by Ihsan 1996 p. 2 ('penelitian bahasa Lematang sebelumnya tidak ada').
